Figure 1.caption: Figure 1. FlowPilot system architecture. User inputs are converted into a chemistry plan and an initial engineering proposal, supported by flow-chemistry literature and handbook knowledge. The seven-agent council generates and reviews candidate designs, records structured verdicts, and proposes bounded revisions. The selected candidate is reconciled with engineering calculations and laboratory inventory before a process-flow diagram, protocol, report, confidence assessment, and supporting citations are returned. The illustrated recipe card is schematic; computational validation does not establish experimental performance.

Figure 2.caption: Figure 2. Literature corpus and engineering rule-base coverage. (e) Category and severity distribution within the 2,537-rule engineering knowledge base. (f) Recorded associations between rule categories and chemistry classes. Full categorical exports and field-specific availability are reported in Figures S3-S4 and Tables S4-S5; associations indicate knowledge coverage rather than independent validation of every rule.

Figure S1.caption: Figure S1. FlowPilot architecture, authority boundaries, and typed data contracts. Figure S2.caption: Figure S2. Standardized intake, GUI execution, synchronized results, and run provenance. (a) The chemist supplies a protocol, resolves context-dependent questions with stable identifiers, and selects inventory. The completed input package is frozen for the current run, while earlier answers remain in history. (b) The schematic GUI supports model selection, progress monitoring, and review, routing consistent designs to results and unresolved requirements to revision. Parameter symbols and the oxygen inlet arrangement are illustrative. (d) Timestamped folders preserve inputs, designs, equipment assignments, topology, and visual artifacts. Computational consistency checks do not constitute experimental validation, and traceable input handling does not guarantee identical model responses.

Table S6.caption: Table S6. Frozen plan-aware retrieval tiers and reranking weights.

Figure S5.caption: Figure S5. Plan-aware retrieval workflow. (a) ChemistryPlan fields enrich the query before semantic retrieval; an embedding-provider failure invokes the deterministic lexical fallback without changing the query or metadata filters. (b) Tiered retrieval starts with paired records and strict mechanism/phase filters, relaxes filters when fewer than three results remain, and expands to all records only when no paired result remains; hidden source identifiers are excluded. (c) Reranking combines 0.60 semantic similarity with 0.40 field similarity before descending top-k selection.
